results.title: Previous work on hallucination analysis has focused on a different kind of correctness, namely if the explanations reflect true world-knowledge (Bang et al., 2023; Yao et al., 2023; Rawte et al., 2023; Lin et al., 2022; Lee et al., 2021). Although important, such analysis can only be applied to self-explanations about facts, not the model’s opinions. It also doesn’t tell us if the self-explanations truly reflect the model’s reasoning process, known as interpretability-faithfulness (Jacovi and Goldberg, 2020; Doshi-Velez and Kim, 2017).

results.title: In this work, we introduce **SELECT** (Selective-abstention Evaluated by Leveraging an Extensive Concept Taxonomy), a benchmark to evaluate the effectiveness, generalization and specificity of abstention techniques. **SELECT** derives benign concepts from a knowledge graph (KG) (Suchanek et al., 2024). By focusing on benign concepts, we intend to isolate the effects of safety-training approaches performed for sensitive topics. Further, the connection with KGs allows us to exploit the hierarchical relations between entities to evaluate generalization and specificity.
